model_interpretation.claim: Combining T1’s capped OpenMP team and 256-options-per-worker cutoff with four-option SSE2 arithmetic may reduce arithmetic overhead on large inputs, but scalar logf/expf calls and interaction with threading may limit or erase the benefit. The combined program needs its own measurement.

model_interpretation.claim: The selected SSE2 parent is valid and measured 5.631 ms versus the 7.529 ms scalar baseline, but its per-lane logf/expf calls may limit SIMD throughput. Replacing those calls with guarded SSE2 polynomial log/exp approximations may reduce that cost while retaining the supplied Black-Scholes formula and CND coefficients. Unsafe input ranges, tails, and builds without SSE2 use the scalar implementation. This tests the remaining scalar-math bottleneck; speed and tolerance compliance remain unmeasured.
